exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

True carnitas from Michoacán are braised low and slow, then crisped to create edges that shatter against tender, pull-apart meat. This technique packs pork tightly in a dish so it braises in its own rendered fat - no vat of lard required. The double-broil finish is non-negotiable: broil, stir, broil again. For a faster weeknight version using ground pork, see [Chipotle Pork Bowls](/mise/recipes/chipotle-pork-and-sweet-corn-tamale-bowls).

## Directions

1.  **Season:** Salt the pork chunks generously. Let sit 30 minutes (or overnight in fridge).
2.  **Arrange:** Preheat oven to 275°F. Pack pork tightly in a 9x13 baking dish. Squeeze orange quarters over meat and nestle them in. Add onion, garlic, bay leaves, and cinnamon. Drizzle oil over top.
3.  **Braise:** Cover tightly with foil. Bake 3-3.5 hours until fork-tender.
4.  **Strain:** Remove aromatics and discard. Drain pork, reserving liquid. Skim fat from liquid and add it back to the meat.
5.  **Shred:** Pull pork into large chunks with two forks. Season with salt.
6.  **Crisp:** Spread on a sheet pan. Broil 6 minutes until edges crisp. Stir. Broil 6 more minutes.
7.  **Elote Sauce:** Mix mayo, sour cream, half the cotija, and chile powder.
8.  **Assemble:** Rice in bowls. Top with carnitas, black beans, charred corn dressed with elote sauce, pickled onions, cabbage, avocado, pepitas, remaining cotija, cilantro, and lime.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Carnitas have a strong association with Michoacán. This oven version keeps the pork close together under a tight cover, then returns its rendered fat to the meat before broiling for crisp edges. Stir once between the two broiler passes so new surfaces face the heat. The rice, beans, pickled onions, charred corn and creamy cotija dressing make this a full bowl; the faster ground-pork [Chipotle Pork Bowls](/mise/recipes/chipotle-pork-and-sweet-corn-tamale-bowls) use a different method.

## Directions

1. **Season and refrigerate:** Use pork shoulder and kosher salt: coat the pork chunks with all the measured initial kosher salt. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or overnight. Do not leave the raw pork seasoning on the counter.
2. **Arrange and braise:** Preheat the oven to 275°F. Put the seasoned pork close together in an oven-safe dish that holds it snugly without a broad empty area; the original 9×13-inch dish suggestion applies only if the actual meat fits that arrangement. Use appropriately fitted dishes for smaller batches or additional snug vessels for larger batches rather than spreading the same meat over an oversized pan. Add orange, yellow onion, garlic cloves, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, and vegetable oil: squeeze the orange over the meat before nestling its quarters, the onion, garlic, bay and cinnamon among the chunks, then drizzle all the oil over the top. Cover tightly with foil or the dish's oven-safe lid. Bake for 3–3½ hours as a starting range, until the meat pulls apart readily with a fork. Check thick pork chunks in more than one area of each vessel reach at least 145°F / 63°C before removing from heat; allow at least 3 minutes rest before cutting or shredding. That minimum temperature alone does not promise pull-apart shoulder.
3. **Strain and return the fat:** Remove and discard the orange quarters, onion, garlic, bay leaves and cinnamon. Strain the pork, reserving all the cooking liquid. Separate the rendered fat from that liquid and return ALL the separated fat to the meat. Keep the remaining cooking juices separately for another preparation. Cool and refrigerate reserved juices promptly in a shallow container if not using them immediately.
4. **Shred and season:** Pull the pork into large pieces with two forks. Taste the cooked meat, then add salt only as needed; the full measured initial salt has already been used.
5. **Crisp in two passes:** Spread the meat and all its returned fat in a single layer on a broiler-safe rimmed metal sheet pan, using additional pans or loads if needed. Broil, starting to check at 6 minutes, until exposed edges crisp; stir so other surfaces face the heat, then broil again, starting to check within another 6 minutes. Watch the meat throughout and stop when the edges are crisp without drying every piece. Broiler strength and load change the timing.
6. **Dress the prepared corn:** Use ears of corn, mayonnaise, sour cream, 1/2 of the cotija cheese, and ancho chile powder: mix all the mayonnaise, sour cream and chile powder with half the measured cotija, reserving the other half for the bowls. Toss this dressing with all the already-charred corn kernels. Keep this corn/dressing refrigerated until assembly if making it ahead.
7. **Build the bowls:** Divide all the carnitas and dressed corn among the planned portions. Add 1/2 of the cotija cheese, [Cilantro Lime Rice](/mise/recipes/cilantro-lime-rice), [Seasoned Black Beans](/mise/recipes/quick-seasoned-black-beans), [Pickled Red Onions](/mise/recipes/pickled-red-onions), green cabbage, avocados, pepitas, fresh cilantro, and limes: use the prepared rice as the base, add the prepared beans and pickled onions in amounts wanted, then distribute all the measured cabbage, avocado, pepitas, remaining cotija and lime wedges across the bowls with the cilantro. The linked recipes have their own batch yields; this bowl does not specify that a full batch of each is needed.

processGraph.title: Season and refrigerate
processGraph.text: Use {{ingredients}}: coat the pork chunks with all the measured initial kosher salt. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or overnight. Do not leave the raw pork seasoning on the counter.

processGraph.title: Arrange and braise
processGraph.text: Preheat the oven to 275°F. Put the seasoned pork close together in an oven-safe dish that holds it snugly without a broad empty area; the original 9×13-inch dish suggestion applies only if the actual meat fits that arrangement. Use appropriately fitted dishes for smaller batches or additional snug vessels for larger batches rather than spreading the same meat over an oversized pan. Add {{ingredients}}: squeeze the orange over the meat before nestling its quarters, the onion, garlic, bay and cinnamon among the chunks, then drizzle all the oil over the top. Cover tightly with foil or the dish's oven-safe lid. Bake for 3–3½ hours as a starting range, until the meat pulls apart readily with a fork. Check thick pork chunks in more than one area of each vessel reach at least 145°F / 63°C before removing from heat; allow at least 3 minutes rest before cutting or shredding. That minimum temperature alone does not promise pull-apart shoulder.

processGraph.title: Strain and return the fat
processGraph.text: Remove and discard the orange quarters, onion, garlic, bay leaves and cinnamon. Strain the pork, reserving all the cooking liquid. Separate the rendered fat from that liquid and return ALL the separated fat to the meat. Keep the remaining cooking juices separately for another preparation. Cool and refrigerate reserved juices promptly in a shallow container if not using them immediately.

processGraph.title: Shred and season
processGraph.text: Pull the pork into large pieces with two forks. Taste the cooked meat, then add {{ingredients}} only as needed; the full measured initial salt has already been used.

processGraph.title: Crisp in two passes
processGraph.text: Spread the meat and all its returned fat in a single layer on a broiler-safe rimmed metal sheet pan, using additional pans or loads if needed. Broil, starting to check at 6 minutes, until exposed edges crisp; stir so other surfaces face the heat, then broil again, starting to check within another 6 minutes. Watch the meat throughout and stop when the edges are crisp without drying every piece. Broiler strength and load change the timing.

processGraph.title: Dress the prepared corn
processGraph.text: Use {{ingredients}}: mix all the mayonnaise, sour cream and chile powder with half the measured cotija, reserving the other half for the bowls. Toss this dressing with all the already-charred corn kernels. Keep this corn/dressing refrigerated until assembly if making it ahead.

processGraph.title: Build the bowls
processGraph.text: Divide all the carnitas and dressed corn among the planned portions. Add {{ingredients}}: use the prepared rice as the base, add the prepared beans and pickled onions in amounts wanted, then distribute all the measured cabbage, avocado, pepitas, remaining cotija and lime wedges across the bowls with the cilantro. The linked recipes have their own batch yields; this bowl does not specify that a full batch of each is needed.

panCapacity: Keep 2-inch pork chunks and a snug covered arrangement at every batch size. A 9×13-inch dish may leave too much empty space for the original 3 lb shoulder; choose its fit after cutting the meat. Use additional snug vessels for larger batches, and keep broiler meat in one layer.
ratiosYieldAndCapacity.clock: With the rice, beans, pickled onions, charred corn and toasted pepitas already prepared, plan about 40 minutes of hands-on seasoning, straining, shredding, dressing and assembly, 30 minutes refrigerated seasoning, 3–3½ hours covered braising, at least 3 minutes rest and roughly 12 minutes of broiling plus heating time: allow about 4–5 hours overall. Some dressing/preparation can overlap the braise. Overnight seasoning is additional advance time, and extra vessels or broiler loads extend the clock. Making the linked preparations or charring corn from scratch is not included in that ready-components estimate.
